 Inspiration 

 Over 70% of houseplants die from overwatering, not neglect. Plant enthusiasts juggle erratic watering schedules, unpredictable weather swings, and perplexing leaf symptoms. Existing plant applications behave like static digital encyclopedias: they provide generic reference text but lack context, cannot inspect local weather, and cannot reason about actual care logs. 

 When OpenAI and the W3C community introduced WebMCP ( document.modelContext.registerTool ), we realized websites no longer need to be passive surfaces where AI agents clumsily guess buttons via computer vision or brittle DOM scraping. We envisioned a web app where an AI agent acts as a genuine gardener: checking live rainfall, cross-referencing care records, diagnosing ailments from physical evidence, and executing care routines—while the human watches the interface update live in real time. 

 
 "Plant apps today are reference books. PlantNeeds is an active gardener." 
 

 What it does 

 PlantNeeds is a full-stack botanical management application natively designed for dual consumption: human interaction via a glassmorphic interface and AI agent interaction via 7 WebMCP tools . 

 1. Dual-Audience Architecture 

 Humans click buttons and monitor dashboards; AI agents (such as ChatGPT in its in-app browser or Chrome with the WebMCP flag) discover and call registered browser tools via document.modelContext.registerTool() . Both share identical backend business logic and database persistence. 

 2. Weather-Adjusted Rain Skipping (Flagship Tool: get_watering_forecast ) 

 Outdoor plants are automatically cross-referenced with live hyperlocal rainfall data (past 7 days + 7-day forecast via Open-Meteo). The agent computes effective precipitation: 

 P eff = P recent + γ ⋅ P forecast 

 Where $\gamma = 0.5$ dampens forecast uncertainty. If $P_{\text{eff}} \ge W_{\text{weekly}}$ (where $W_{\text{weekly}}$ is the species' weekly water demand), the recommendation emits:
 Verdict = SKIP ( "Rain already covered outdoor beds" ) 
Indoor plants are automatically isolated from rainfall logic. 

 3. History-Aware Plant Problem Diagnosis ( diagnose_problem ) 

 Instead of static symptom lookup tables, PlantNeeds scores candidate causes against actual care history stored in PostgreSQL: 

 S ( C ) = B ( C , symptoms ) + ∑ k w k ⋅ I ( Condition k ) 

 If a plant presents with yellow leaves and drooping, but care logs show:
 Δ t interval < f recommended ∧ drainage = false 
The likelihood of root rot / overwatering surges above 90%, citing concrete evidence rather than generic guesses. 

 4. Interactive Care Scheduling & Growth Tracking ( get_care_schedule , log_care_activity , log_growth ) 

 Urgency is continuously ranked:
 U ( p ) = Δ t since f water − 1 
When $U(p) \ge 0$, the plant is flagged overdue. When the agent logs care ( source: 'agent' ), countdown timers reset instantly. 

 5. Reactive Live-Sync Animation 

 When the AI agent performs an action through WebMCP, PostgreSQL records the mutation, the client store refetches state, and the UI triggers an Agent Pulse ripple animation and a notification toast ( 🤖 Monstera deliciosa watered by agent ) without refreshing the page. 

 How we built it 

 We implemented PlantNeeds around strict separation of concerns, ensuring zero duplicated logic between human and AI interfaces: 
 ┌──────────────────────┐ ┌────────────────────────┐
 │ Human Web UI │ │ WebMCP Agent Layer │
 │ Buttons, Modals │ │ 7 × registerTool() │
 └──────────┬───────────┘ └───────────┬────────────┘
 │ UI Events │ Tool Execution
 └────────────────┬────────────────┘
 ▼
 ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Client Logic & Event Bus │
 │ (Vite + Reactive Pub/Sub) │
 └────────────────┬────────────────┘
 │ HTTP REST + JWT
 ▼
 ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Server Logic Engine (Pure) │
 │ (Node.js / Express Middleware) │
 └────────────────┬────────────────┘
 │ Parameterized SQL
 ▼
 ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
 │ PostgreSQL (Render Managed) │
 │ Users, Plants, Care & Growth │
 └─────────────────────────────────┘
 
 
 WebMCP Integration ( client/src/tools/register-tools.js ) : Guarded by runtime feature detection ( 'modelContext' in document ). Each tool defines strict JSON Schema validation, semantic input parameters, and descriptive prompts optimized for LLM tool-calling routers. 
 Backend & Logic Engine ( server/logic/ ) : Pure functions isolated from transport handlers:

 
 plants.js : Care schedule calculation and CRUD mutations. 
 weather.js : Open-Meteo proxy with a 30-minute PostgreSQL caching table to avoid API rate limits. 
 diagnose.js : 20-cause symptom matrix combined with historical timeline heuristics. 
 planner.js : Companion planting rules and seasonal frost-date calendars. 
 
 Frontend Reactive Store ( client/src/state/store.js ) : Custom micro pub/sub bus triggering targeted DOM updates and glassmorphic micro-interactions. 
 Visual Design : Botanical Ether Glassmorphism (semi-transparent frosted glass rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.22) , blur filters, Forest Deep #1B3022 palette, Plus Jakarta Sans, and JetBrains Mono). 
 

 Challenges we ran into 

 
 Prompt Engineering as AI UX (Constraint C7) : Early browser agent tests picked incorrect tools or omitted parameters. We learned that tool descriptions are the "UI for LLMs." Formulating explicit usage triggers, defining enum values, and clarifying sibling differences (e.g. routine care log_care_activity vs milestone journal log_growth ) brought agent tool selection to 100% reliability. 
 Headless & In-App Browser Geolocation : In the ChatGPT in-ap

live_observation.first_impression: PlantNeeds presents a login screen with username/email and password fields plus Google, sign-in, and account-creation controls.
live_observation.after_state: A registration form appeared requesting optional full name, username/email, password, and confirmation; no account was created.
live_observation.notes: The plant-care functionality was behind authentication; no credentials or personal data were entered.
